title: Why Do We Kiss?
beats: Kiss stats and world record, then why do we do it; the first kissers might have been gross
Begins with what is known: kissing feels good and is healthy
Asks why brains that love kissing became common
Pacman pizza story is only half true; mouths and eating link to kiss
Kiss-feeding: birds and primates pass pre-chewed food mouth to mouth
Silverstone clip and the nutrition benefits of saliva
Mouth contact as intimacy, and saliva as a taste test for a mate
Selection story: kissers chose better mates and became the norm
Infant vision range matches mother's face; why humans see faces
Pareidolia; white sclera and gaze-direction neurons
Psychic staring effect is pseudo-science; rubbernecking explains it
Is love for mother just food? Introduces wire mother
Harlow's cloth versus wire mothers; monkeys cling to cloth when scared; ethics noted
Rejecting mother and shocked ducklings attach more tightly
Fisher's three puppy groups: kind, punishing, random; random group most attached
Polarity Principle named; we are the third group of puppies
Uncertainty to knowledge: a taste-test kiss only matters if the mate matters

metrics.misconception: yes: attachment comes from food (6:18); psychic staring (5:39)
metrics.examples: about 6; grows from kiss-feeding to monkeys to ducklings to puppies, and gets darker
metrics.ending: Ties uncertainty back to why a kiss feels good, then a plain kiss prompt

new_moves.name: paradox-chain
new_moves.what: Stacks the same counterintuitive result across species to build a pattern the viewer can state

new_moves.name: ethics-flag
new_moves.what: Names the unethical history of an experiment right as it is introduced

new_moves.name: two-stories-in-one
new_moves.what: Two threads (kissing, attachment) run in parallel and merge in the last minute

theory: The video lets a surprising result repeat in three species until the learner has the rule themselves, then names it. The weak point is the leap from puppies to kissing, which is argued by rhetoric.
velocity: Playbook: paradox-chain, with the same counterintuitive result shown in successive examples before naming the principle
Evals: flag a final bridge that asserts instead of demonstrates
Scene builder: render the two-mothers cage as a literal toy world and let the learner predict where the monkey goes
quote: a paradox is the truth standing on its head to attract attention.
